text:
Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: A generic institutional records office files ordinary paperwork by registering each document under a unique identifier, stamping it with a date and the responsible account, and routing it through a defined approval channel before filing it in the permanent ledger.

2) What occurred: The actor submitted a part-history document for a passenger aircraft showing a replacement of a certified component with an uncertified variant. The actor altered the part-identification field to match the original certified part number. The actor modified the installation-date field to predate the uncertified installation. The actor created a maintenance record listing the uncertified part as the original certified part. The actor routed the altered documents through the approval channel using the maintenance supervisor account. The actor marked the documents as airworthiness-approved in the status field. The actor filed the documents in the permanent ledger under the aircraft registration.

3) Materials/access observed: The actor used the maintenance management system account of a licensed engineer. The actor had read and write access to the part-history database. The actor had access to the document-approval workflow. The actor had access to the permanent records ledger. The actor used a named account with elevated filing privileges.

4) Indicators & artifacts: The part-history document shows a component serial that does not match any manufacturer shipment record. The installation-date field predates the component's manufacturing date by a named number of days. The maintenance record references a part number that does not exist in the current catalog. The approval channel log shows the document was approved by the supervisor account during a period when that account was inactive. The permanent ledger entry lacks the required quality-control verification stamp. The document metadata shows the file was edited by the named engineer account after initial submission.
